Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation did not lower depression scores compared with placebo in healthy women over winter.
Sentence: "We found no evidence of lower depression (P = 0·339), lower anxiety (P = 0·862), higher flourishing (P = 0·453), higher positive moods (P = 0·518) or lower negative moods (P = 0·538) in the treatment group compared with the control group at follow-up."
Measured as: depression (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale)
Population: 152 healthy women aged 18-40 years in Dunedin, New Zealand
Intervention: 50 000 IU oral vitamin D3 once per month for 6 months
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with COPD and insufficient vitamin D had higher depression scores (BDI) than those with normal vitamin D levels.
Sentence: "BDI was higher in the InsVD, and this group had a higher risk of developing moderate and severe depression (OR=3.37; 95% CI=0.895, 12.722; p=0.03)."
Measured as: depression (BDI)
Population: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with normal (n=24) or insufficient (n=7) vitamin D levels
Intervention: Vitamin D status (insufficient vs normal), observational, no intervention given
Comparator: Normal vitamin D levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 31
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"A placebo-controlled trial in healthy women found no effect of supplementation, while a small cross-sectional study in COPD patients found higher depression scores with insufficient vitamin D; the results diverge mainly by design and population.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"RCT of monthly 50,000 IU D3 vs placebo (n=152, healthy women) against cross-sectional observational association (n=31, COPD patients, BDI)"}
